claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr oxidizes rapidly in air at 800–1000 °C over 5 hours.
Uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes pesting under the stated air-exposure conditions.
The proposed intervention is a 50–100 nm Al2O3 coating deposited by atomic layer deposition on the as-cast alloy.
Applying the proposed ALD Al2O3 coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
ALD will produce a continuous and conformal nanoscale Al2O3 layer on the alloy.
The nanoscale Al2O3 layer will adhere tightly to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature exposure.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a physical barrier that reduces oxygen diffusion to the reactive alloy substrate.
Reducing oxygen transport to the substrate will inhibit rapid oxide-scale formation and propagation.
The coating-mediated reduction in oxygen transport will inhibit pesting.
A surface-deposited Al2O3 coating will not alter the alloy's bulk microstructure.
Coated specimens will have significantly lower oxidation mass gain than uncoated specimens after approximately 5 hours in air at 800–1000 °C.
Coated specimens will exhibit less pesting than uncoated specimens after approximately 5 hours in air at 800–1000 °C.
The coating will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility and 1000 °C yield strength at levels similar to those of uncoated material.
The protective effect may fail if mechanical deformation compromises coating integrity.
The proposed protection may not persist at temperatures significantly above 1000 °C or for exposures substantially longer than 5 hours.
The long-term adhesion and stability of the ultrathin coating under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are uncertain.
The coating may affect surface-induced fatigue behavior.
